title: THE LIGHT THAT WENT DARK: Why Revelation 18:23 Feels Uncomfortably Personal
paragraphs: THE LIGHT THAT WENT DARK: Why Revelation 18:23 Feels Uncomfortably Personal
“The deception didn’t begin with darkness… it began with light that looked like truth.”
There is something haunting about a light that disappears.
Not flickering. Not dimming. Gone.
Like a house that once held laughter, now silent. Like a heart that once burned for God, now numb. Like a soul that once knew truth… now unable to recognise it.
Revelation 18:23 doesn’t shout. It whispers. And that’s what makes it terrifying.

“καὶ φῶς λύχνου οὐ μὴ φανῇ ἐν σοὶ ἔτι…”
“And the light of a lamp shall not shine in you anymore…”

The Greek word for light here is φῶς (phōs) — not just physical brightness, but illumination, truth, divine clarity. The kind of light that reveals what is hidden. The kind of light that exposes what we try to bury.
And then there’s λύχνος (lychnos) — a lamp. Not the sun. Not overwhelming glory. Just a steady, personal light. The kind you carry with you. The kind meant to guide your steps.
And God says… it will be gone.
Not taken from a city alone.
But from a people who chose something else.

“…καὶ φωνὴ νυμφίου καὶ νύμφης οὐ μὴ ἀκουσθῇ…”
“And the voice of the bridegroom and bride shall not be heard in you anymore…”
Silence where covenant once lived.
The Bridegroom — Χριστός (Christos). Jesus Himself. The One who calls, who woos, who waits.
Gone.
Not because He stopped speaking.
But because they stopped listening.
This verse is not just about Babylon as a system. It is about what happens when a heart becomes so saturated with illusion that truth sounds foreign.

“…ὅτι οἱ ἔμποροί σου ἦσαν οἱ μεγάλοι τῆς γῆς…”
“For your merchants were the great ones of the earth…”
The Greek word ἔμποροι (emporoi) refers to traders, dealers, influencers of exchange. Not just sellers of goods… but shapers of desire.
People who decide what matters.
People who make the temporary feel eternal.
People who turn souls into transactions.
And then comes the line that cuts deeper than most are willing to admit:

“…ὅτι ἐν τῇ φαρμακείᾳ σου ἐπλανήθησαν πάντα τὰ ἔθνη.”
“For by your sorcery all nations were deceived.”
The word is φαρμακεία (pharmakeia).
It’s where we get “pharmacy”… but don’t misunderstand it. This is not about medicine. It is about manipulation. Enchantment. Spiritual intoxication.
It is the altering of perception.
It is making people feel awake… while they are asleep.
It is giving them something that numbs conviction while amplifying desire.
It is distraction dressed as pleasure.
Illusion dressed as truth.
And the nations — πάντα τὰ ἔθνη (panta ta ethnē) — all peoples, all cultures, all backgrounds…
Deceived.
Not forced.
Deceived.
That means they didn’t realise it.
That means it felt normal.
That means it felt right.
That means it might feel right to you too.
That’s the part we don’t like to sit with.
Because it raises a question that doesn’t leave you alone:
What if the thing you’ve normalised… is the very thing dimming your light?
What if the silence in your spirit isn’t because God left…
…but because something else got louder?
You see, Revelation 18 is not just prophecy.
It is exposure.
Exposure of a system that profits from your disconnection from God.
Exposure of a culture that thrives when truth feels optional.
Exposure of a world that celebrates everything except repentance.
And somewhere in the middle of all of that…
you are still being called.
Not by noise.
But by a voice that refuses to stop pursuing you.
In Hebrew, light is אוֹר (’or) — the same word used in Genesis when God said, “Let there be light.”
“יְהִי אוֹר (Yehi ’or).”
That light wasn’t just physical. It was order over chaos. Truth over confusion. Life over emptiness.
And the same God who spoke light into existence…
is still trying to speak light into you.
But light requires something uncomfortable.
Exposure.
And that’s where many walk away.
Because darkness doesn’t fight back when you hide in it.
But light?
Light shows you what you’ve been avoiding.
Light reveals what you’ve been protecting.
Light confronts what you’ve been justifying.
So people choose dimness.
They choose distraction.
They choose anything that keeps them from hearing the voice of the Bridegroom clearly.
And slowly…
the lamp goes out.
Not in a moment.
But in compromises.
In distractions.
In “it’s not that serious.”
Until one day…
you realise you can’t feel Him like you used to.
And that silence feels heavier than anything you’ve ever carried.
But here is the part that changes everything.
Jesus does not expose to destroy.
He exposes to restore.
Because even in Revelation, the warning is mercy.
Even in judgment, there is invitation.
Even in the darkness, there is still a call:
“Come out of her, my people…”
Not “run from Me.”
Not “you’re too far gone.”
But “come out.”
Come back.
Come home.
And maybe that’s why this verse feels so personal.
Because deep down…
you know when your light isn’t burning the way it used to.
You know when something has taken His place.
You know when your heart feels distant.
So be honest.
Not with me.
With Him.
Because it did.
And if it did…
someone you love needs this too.
but because it might be the wake-up call someone never knew they needed.
Not to judge them.
But to remind them that the light is still calling them back.
Because there will be a moment when your spirit feels numb again…
and you’ll need to remember what truth felt like.
but truth that actually confronts, heals, and restores.
And if you are serious about going deeper…
about not just hearing truth but living it…
then step into something stronger.
they grow deeper.
They walk closer.
They fight stronger.
If you truly want to glorify God…
don’t just consume truth.
Support the mission that spreads it.
Because someone’s eternity might be one shared post away.
And maybe…
just maybe…
so was yours.
The light doesn’t disappear all at once… it fades wherever truth is replaced.
